string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing, the capital of China, is a major political, cultural and educational centre in East Asia. It has served as an imperial capital for centuries, most notably under the Ming and Qing dynasties, and today contains world-famous heritage sites such as the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven and the Great Wall. The city hosted the 2008 and 2022 Olympic Games and is home to many top universities, research institutes and state-owned enterprises. Its combination of ancient palaces, modern skyscrapers and a fast-growing technology sector makes it one of the most influential cities in the world.

Shanghai is the largest city in China and a leading global financial centre. Located on the Yangtze River delta, it grew from a fishing village into a major treaty port in the nineteenth century and has since become a hub of commerce, shipping and innovation. The Bund, with its colonial-era buildings facing the modern Pudong skyline, is one of the most recognisable views in Asia. Shanghai also has a lively cultural scene, hosting international art exhibitions, film festivals and fashion events, and its metro system is among the longest in the world, connecting a diverse population of more than twenty-four million people.

Chongqing, formerly romanized as Chungking, is a major municipality in southwest China and one of the fastest-growing urban areas in the country. It sits at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers, and its dramatic mountainous terrain has earned it the nickname Mountain City. During the Second World War it served as the wartime capital of China. Today it is a key industrial base and inland port, especially for automobiles, electronics and logistics, and it is famous for its spicy hotpot, the Three Gorges Dam nearby and the Hongya Cave night views along the river.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality and an important port city in northern China, located on the Bohai Sea not far from Beijing. It developed rapidly in the nineteenth century as a trading port and retains a remarkable collection of European-style architecture in the Five Great Avenues area. The city is home to Nankai and Tianjin universities, a major aerospace and advanced manufacturing sector, and the modern Tianjin Binhai New Area. Its coastal setting, historic streets and economic ties to Beijing make it a significant centre of trade, education and industry in northern China.
